task.name: Dependency Review Bypass Remediation
task.description: Review merged pull requests that changed dependency manifests or lockfiles and surface only changes for which the repository's required dependency-review check did not produce an accepted result before merge, without reopening an already tracked or explicitly accepted exception.
task.intent: Reduce operator time spent discovering and remediating merged dependency changes that bypassed required dependency review while avoiding duplicate attention and remaining distinct from protected-branch control bypass.
activationConditions: A pull request merged within the evidence window changes a dependency manifest, lockfile, or supported dependency snapshot in a covered repository.
Authoritative pull request, check-run, and repository dependency-review policy evidence shows the required dependency-review check had no accepted result for that dependency change before merge.
requiredEffects: Each novel finding identifies the merged pull request, changed dependency evidence, applicable dependency-review requirement, and check-run evidence proving that an accepted dependency-review result was absent before merge.
Maintainers can accept, reject, or resolve each surfaced finding using repository-linked evidence without treating the finding as a protected-branch bypass.
noopConditions: Every merged dependency change in scope had an accepted dependency-review result before merge.
Every supported dependency-review bypass finding for the covered merged changes is already tracked or explicitly accepted.
successConditions: Supported dependency-review bypass findings receive accepted remediation evidence or an explicit maintainer dismissal within 14 days of the workflow run.
Merged dependency changes with accepted dependency-review results create no duplicate maintainer attention.
uncertainties: A repository may accept a documented emergency dependency update without a pre-merge dependency-review result while still requiring explicit maintainer acceptance evidence.
Renamed manifests, generated lockfiles, or unsupported package ecosystems may make dependency-change classification incomplete and must not be inferred as a protected-branch bypass.

operationalValue.statement: The proportion of supported, novel dependency-review bypass findings assigned to the run that are resolved or explicitly dismissed within 14 days.
operationalValue.opportunity: One workflow run and the deduplicated supported dependency-review bypass findings it assigns for covered merged dependency changes.
acceptedEvidence: A merged follow-up pull request with an accepted dependency-review result that reverts, replaces, or revalidates the identified dependency change before the evidence cutoff.
A closed tracking issue, pull request conversation, or repository-linked exception record that explicitly marks the dependency-review bypass finding resolved, dismissed, or accepted by a maintainer.
evidenceRepositories: The repository containing the merged dependency change and in which the workflow ran.

metric.name: resolved-supported-dependency-review-bypass-findings
metric.formula: resolved-or-dismissed supported dependency-review bypass findings / supported novel dependency-review bypass findings assigned to the run

operationalValue.maturation: 14 days after the workflow run completes.
operationalValue.zeroRule: Return 0 when at least one supported novel dependency-review bypass finding was assigned and none has accepted resolution evidence by the evidence cutoff.
operationalValue.missingRule: Return null when the assigned finding set or required pull request, dependency-change, check-run, or dependency-review policy evidence cannot be read.

rows.finding-summary: Merged pull request 201 changed package-lock.json, policy required dependency-review/action, and no accepted check result existed before merge.

rows.outcome-summary: Merged follow-up change revalidated the dependency with an accepted dependency-review result.
